mainProgression.description: A textbook classical descending bassline (A - G# - F# - E - D) providing heartbreaking voice-leading

sectionProgressions.progression: A - E/G# - F#m - A/E - D/F# - E7 - A
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - V/3 - vi - I/5 - IV/3 - V7 - I
sectionProgressions.description: The signature descending bass fingerpicking sequence underpinning the vocal reflection
Circle-of-fifths diatonic progression asking 'Would you know my name?'

sectionProgressions.progression: C - G/B - Am - D/F# - G - D/F# - Em - D
sectionProgressions.description: Temporary modulation to C major / G major expressing grief and resilience ('Time can bring you down')

harmonicFunction: Descending stepwise bassline A → G# → F# → E → D creates an inescapable feeling of emotional gravity
First inversion slash chords (E/G#, D/F#) smooth out chord changes into continuous linear counterpoint
Suspension on E7sus4 delays the final resolution to A, heightening vulnerability
Bridge modulation to the flat-mediant C major introduces bittersweet dramatic tension

techniques.name: Classical Nylon-String Fingerpicking
techniques.description: PIMA right-hand fingerstyle technique balancing independent basslines with simultaneous treble chord plucks

notes: Clapton played a custom Juan Alvarez nylon-string classical guitar on the recording
Thumb (P) strictly controls strings 6, 5, and 4; index (I), middle (M), and ring (A) pluck strings 3, 2, and 1
Right-hand fingernails or fleshy fingertips provide warm, intimate tone
sequence: Thumb plucks root bass note on downbeat
Fingers simultaneously pluck treble strings on the 'and' of the beat
Thumb steps down to the next descending bass note on beat 2
tips: Keep the right hand arched comfortably over the soundhole
Do not anchor your pinky finger on the guitar top; keep hand floating freely

techniques.name: Thumb-Over Slash Chords
techniques.description: Wrapping the fretting hand thumb around the neck to fret bass notes (G# on E/G# and F# on D/F#)

notes: Thumb frets the 4th fret on the low E string for E/G# and 2nd fret for D/F#
Allows index, middle, and ring fingers to remain dedicated to treble chord voices
Essential for smooth transitions without jumping fretting hand positions
sequence: Fret A barre or open A shape
Reach thumb over top of fretboard to grab 4th fret low E string
Transition into F#m barre or open grip
tips: Keep the thumb relaxed and flat against the edge of the fretwire
If thumb-over is uncomfortable, use index finger on 4th fret and ring/pinky on upper strings

sections.name: Intro Motif
sections.description: The iconic opening acoustic fingerstyle motif establishing the descending bassline and gentle hammer-on fills.
sections.progression: A - E/G# - F#m - A/E - D/F# - E7 - A
notes: Pluck bass note cleanly on beat 1 with thumb
Execute the subtle hammer-on from open B to C# on the 2nd string
Let the low A string ring through as the foundation of the turnaround

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Delicate fingerpicked accompaniment supporting Clapton's tender vocal delivery.
sections.progression: I - V/3 - vi - I/5 - IV/3 - V7sus4 - V7 - I
notes: Maintain smooth, even volume across all six strings
Accent the stepwise descending bassline on the downbeats
Add slight vibrato on sustained notes for vocal resonance

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Lifting into the emotional questions ('Would you know my name?') moving through C#m, F#m, and Bm7.
notes: Use full barre chord grips on C#m and F#m
Pluck bass note with thumb followed by three-finger pinch on the higher strings
Decrescendo into the delicate resolution back to A major

sections.name: Bridge
sections.description: Dramatic dynamic expansion as the song modulates to C major ('Time can bring you down, time can bend your knees').
sections.progression: C - G/B - Am - D/F# - G - D/F# - Em - D
notes: Strum with slightly more attack to match the emotional peak
Accurately articulate the moving bass notes B and F#
Smooth transition back into A major for the acoustic guitar solo

guitar.recommended: Juan Alvarez Nylon String Classical or Martin 000-42 Acoustic
guitar.pickup: Under-saddle piezo blended with Neumann KM84 small diaphragm condenser

amp.recommended: Pristine Studio Microphone Preamp into Mixing Console

effects.reverb: Warm hall or studio plate reverb with 2.2s decay
effects.other: Subtle optical studio compressor (LA-2A style) for gentle dynamic smoothing

beginner.title: Chord Shapes & Stepwise Bass Line
steps: Learn the basic shapes for A, E/G#, F#m, and D/F#
Practice the descending bassline notes (A, G#, F#, E, D) in isolation
Play simple downstrums on the beat at 60 BPM

intermediate.title: PIMA Fingerpicking Coordination
steps: Develop independent right-hand thumb control on the lower three strings
Synchronize treble finger pinches on the upper three strings with the bass pulse
Incorporate the intro hammer-on flourishes seamlessly

advanced.title: Full Arrangement & Dynamic Expression
steps: Master the bridge modulation through C, G/B, and Am without hesitation
Learn the delicate acoustic nylon-string solo fills
Perform the full piece with expressive rubato and nuanced touch dynamics

commonMistakes: Plucking the treble strings too forcefully relative to the subtle bass voice
Collapsing the fretting hand wrist when fretting the E/G# thumb-over chord
Rushing through the E7sus4 to E7 suspension turnaround
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Right-hand fingerstyle independence warm-ups on open strings
10 min: Slow repetition of the descending bassline transitions at 60 BPM
10 min: Bridge modulation practice with metronome at 80 BPM
focusAreas: Smooth descending voice-leading clarity in the bass
Touch sensitivity and acoustic tone control
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 60 BPM with quarter-note clicks to build fingerstyle precision
Slowly increase by 4 BPM intervals up to target recording tempo of 80 BPM
Practice playing slightly behind the beat for an intimate, relaxed feel
